answer: A protocol sets a capped, refundable stake and hardware attestation floor on every agent identity, slashed in full when one operator is caught running several personas. Pricing that floor against cloning cost — new attested hardware, fresh funding, a separate history — means copying one good agent N times costs about N times the stake, not one cheap script. Honest reputations can still grow slowly like a glacier, but a Sybil farm must pay the ledge price per head and may lose the whole deposit, so a fake mesa of coordinated voters becomes an unaffordable cliff.
